home.title: 🌳 LiDAR Biomass Prediction
home.metric_plots_help: ≥ 99.9% of its area within one contiguous campaign
home.pipeline_caption: Click the steps to walk through the flow.

pipeline_steps.title: Download LiDAR
pipeline_steps.desc: Download of the airborne LiDAR tiles (NASA/ORNL CMS Brazil): .laz point clouds covering Amazon areas across different campaigns and years. It is one of the two raw sources of the project and runs in parallel with the inventory download.

pipeline_steps.title: Download inventory
pipeline_steps.desc: Download of the field forest inventories: .csv files with tree-by-tree measurements (diameter, height, species) and .kmz files with plot geometry. It is the second raw source and serves as ground truth for biomass.

pipeline_steps.title: Extract KML
pipeline_steps.desc: Conversion of the inventory .kmz files into KML, isolating the polygon of each field plot. This clean geometry is what enables the spatial cross-reference of plots with LiDAR tiles in the next step.

pipeline_steps.title: Find intersections
pipeline_steps.desc: Spatial cross-reference between plots and tiles: each plot with ≥ 99.9% of its area inside one campaign's contiguous coverage (neighboring same-flight tiles merged) is kept. For each plot the temporal gap between the LiDAR flight and the field measurement is computed, keeping the campaign with the smallest year difference.

pipeline_steps.title: Clip point cloud
pipeline_steps.desc: Clipping of each selected tile's point cloud to the exact plot polygon, producing one isolated .laz file per plot. It is the direct input to the prediction model.

pipeline_steps.title: Inventory biomass
pipeline_steps.desc: Estimation of each plot's above-ground biomass (AGB) directly from the field inventory, applying allometric equations (Chave, Chambers, Goodman) tree by tree and summing per plot. This branch starts from the inventory, independent of LiDAR.

pipeline_steps.title: Estimation model
pipeline_steps.desc: Training a model that learns AGB from the clipped point clouds. The two branches converge here: each plot's point cloud is the predictor and the inventory biomass is the target. Once calibrated, the model can estimate biomass over any LiDAR-covered area, even without inventory: the project's final goal.

map.title: LiDAR × Inventory Coverage Map
map.intro_map: The map shows the overlap between forest inventory plots and LiDAR tiles. Each marker is a plot: **red** when ≥ 99.9% of its area is covered by one campaign’s contiguous coverage (neighboring same-flight tiles merged) and **gray** otherwise. Blue rectangles are the LiDAR tiles actually used. Use the layer control at the top right to toggle each set; zoom in to see the plot polygons.
map.table_intro: The table summarizes each inventory site: how many distinct LiDAR tiles cover it, how many plots the site has in the inventory, how many of those are ≥ 99.9% covered by a campaign and, in the last column, the count keeping only the best temporal match — the campaign whose flight year is closest to the inventory year.
map.legend_caption: Marker colour = plot usability. **Green**: has LiDAR + biomass → trains a model. **Red**: overlaps LiDAR but no biomass assignable to the polygon. **Gray**: no LiDAR overlap. (Same partition as the 'What reaches the models' chart.)
map.design_note_title: Why do some red plots have no polygon or label?
map.design_note:
Not every red plot is a data error — it usually reflects the **field inventory design**:

- **Nested subplots.** Several sites place, inside each ~50×50 m square (main plot, ~0.25 ha), a **narrow ~5×50 m strip** (~0.025 ha — 1/10 of the area) along an inner edge. The strip samples a **smaller size class** (small stems, regeneration). When the inventory only measured the large trees of the square, the strip has **no trees → no biomass → red**. Example: **SAN_A02_2014**, strips 8–14 (red) vs. squares 1–7 (green).
- **Linear transects.** Some sites (**TAP_A01/A04/A05**) record the plot as a ~500 m **line**, with no width — no area to clip and no pairable label. That is why they appear as a **line** on the map rather than a polygon.

intersections.title: Intersection Analysis
intersections.all_caption: Plot × LiDAR campaign pairs, no temporal filter
intersections.best_caption: One LiDAR campaign per plot — the smallest gap
intersections.intro: A single plot can fall inside more than one LiDAR tile, flown in different years. Here we analyze the time difference (*temporal gap*) between the LiDAR acquisition and the field inventory: the smaller the gap, the more reliable it is to pair the two sources.
intersections.all_desc: Distribution of **all** plot × LiDAR-campaign **pairs** (**{n}** pairs). The same plot appears multiple times when flown in distinct campaigns — the full supply of combinations by gap.
intersections.best_desc: Distribution with **one row per plot** (**{n}** plots), keeping only the smallest-gap LiDAR campaign. This is the set we actually use: each plot's best temporal match.
intersections.chart_note: In both charts the bars are colored by gap band (same year, ≤ 2 years, > 2 years) and the X axis is the gap in years. Both use the same scale for direct comparison.
intersections.coverage_intro: Not every inventory plot makes it into the study. We require ≥ 99.9% of the plot's area to lie within the **contiguous coverage of one campaign** (neighboring tiles from the same flight, merged; a/b subcampaigns of the same year count as one) — so it is covered by a homogeneous cloud without mixing acquisitions. The metrics below show how many plots survive each filter and how many source files were corrupted.
intersections.cov_kept_help: ≥ 99.9% of the plot area within a campaign's contiguous coverage (neighbouring tiles of the same flight, merged). This is **geometric** coverage — not every covered plot has biomass to train on (see "What reaches the models").
intersections.cov_discarded_help: Touch a tile but have less than 99.9% of their area within one campaign’s coverage.
intersections.cov_no_overlap_help: Do not touch any LiDAR tile, not even partially.
intersections.cov_corrupt_pc_help: Used .laz tiles that failed to read during clipping.
intersections.cov_corrupt_inv_help: Plot KMLs that failed to read.
intersections.usable_intro: Overlapping the LiDAR is only the first filter. To **train a model** a plot needs three things: LiDAR overlap, a clipped cloud, and a **biomass label** (trees measured and assignable to the polygon). Not every covered area has that — a geometric intersection is not the same as a usable plot.
intersections.usable_caption: Of {total} inventory plots, {overlap} overlap the LiDAR; of those, {green} are usable (green) and {red} are excluded for lacking biomass assignable to the polygon (red — e.g. a polygon drawn with no measured trees). {gray} have no LiDAR overlap (gray).

geometry.title: Plot Geometry
geometry.caption: Only plots with LiDAR coverage (≥ 99.9% campaign coverage) and valid polygon geometries.
geometry.help_expander: Mean vs. Median — which to use?
geometry.compactness_caption: Compactness = 4π × area / perimeter²  ·  Circle = 1.0  ·  Square ≈ 0.785  ·  Irregular shapes < 0.5
geometry.intro: Each plot is a polygon. Two properties affect LiDAR-clipping quality: **area** (very small plots contain few points) and **compactness** (how close to a circle the shape is — low values mean thin, elongated shapes that are more sensitive to edge errors when clipping).
geometry.area_desc: Distribution of plot area. The solid red line marks the mean and the dashed line the median; the gap between them indicates skew in the distribution.
geometry.compactness_desc: Compactness = 4π · area / perimeter². It equals 1.0 for a perfect circle, ≈ 0.785 for a square, and tends to 0 for very thin, elongated rectangles.
geometry.shapes_desc: On the left, the most elongated plot in the set (lowest compactness); on the right, the most compact one (highest compactness). Axes are in meters and on the same scale, so the difference in shape stands out.

outliers.title: Geometry Outliers
outliers.caption: Plots with atypical shape or area — thin elongated strips (low compactness) or very large areas. These are the most sensitive to edge error when clipping the LiDAR.
outliers.intro: Each inventory plot is a polygon. Two properties hurt point-cloud clipping quality: very low **compactness** (elongated shapes, where a small edge shift greatly changes the sampled area) and very large **area** (mixed conditions within a single sample). Here you can isolate those cases, see each shape and its numbers — a starting point to decide between **subdividing**, **segmenting** or **excluding** the plot.
outliers.comp_help: Compactness = 4π·area/perimeter². Circle = 1.0 · square ≈ 0.785 · thin strip → 0. Plots below this value are flagged.
outliers.area_help: Plots with area above this value are flagged (too large for a homogeneous sample).
outliers.count: **{n}** of {total} plots flagged as outliers by the current criterion.
outliers.none: No plot meets the current criterion — loosen the thresholds above.
outliers.pick: Plot (sorted from least to most compact)
outliers.shape_note: Real plot shape, in meters and 1:1 aspect. Very thin, long strips (high aspect) are hard to clip without edge error and won't yield square cells when subdivided.
outliers.m_dims_help: Sides of the minimum-area rectangle enclosing the plot (shorter × longer side), in meters.
outliers.m_pos_help: % of the plot's trees whose UTM coordinate falls inside the polygon. Low = missing positions or wrong UTM zone → position-based subdivision unfeasible.
outliers.table_caption: Trees = number of inventory trees assigned to the plot (biomass summary). Reliable pos. = % of those trees falling inside the polygon. "—" when no trees are recorded for the plot.

pointcloud.title: Point Cloud Viewer
pointcloud.caption: Points clipped for each inventory plot. Colored by height (Z).
pointcloud.no_data: No clipped .laz file found in `data/processed/03_clipped_lidar/`. Run `make clip` first.
pointcloud.show_trees_help: Draws a vertical line at the (UTM) position of each field-measured tree that falls inside the plot polygon, from the ground up to the tree height (measured Htot; if missing, Feldpausch-estimated). Useful to compare the inventory structure with the LiDAR cloud.
pointcloud.show_cloud_help: Uncheck to hide the point cloud and see only the tree heights (red lines), for a cleaner view.
pointcloud.height_source_help: Current estimate: field-measured height, else local/Feldpausch fit. Gap-corrected: grows DBH to the LiDAR flight year (increment from re-measurement where available, else mean) and re-derives height — aligns the estimate to the LiDAR date.
pointcloud.trees_caption: Red lines: {n} field inventory trees inside the plot (UTM position, ground to top). Compare with the LiDAR canopy.
pointcloud.trees_noheight_note: The {n} gray markers (×) at ground level are trees WITHOUT a measured or estimable height (no Htot and no DBH) — not fallen trees, just missing height data.
pointcloud.gap_help: Difference in years between the LiDAR flight and this plot's field measurement.
pointcloud.biomass_unavailable: Biomass not available for this plot in summary.csv.
pointcloud.dims_caption: Width × length of the minimum bounding rectangle of the plot polygon (inventory data).

biomass.title: Biomass Analysis
biomass.caption: AGB estimates (Mg/ha) per allometric formula, derived from the field inventory.
biomass.no_data: summary.csv not found in `data/processed/05_biomass/`. Run the biomass pipeline first.
biomass.region_chart_title: AGB per plot (one bar per plot)
biomass.comparison_m1m2: **M1 vs M2** — effect of including height
biomass.diff_header: Mean absolute difference between formulas by site
biomass.intro: Above-ground biomass (AGB, in Mg/ha) estimated from the field inventory using three allometric formulas (M1–M3). Each plot gets one estimate per formula.
biomass.region_desc: Each row is an individual **plot** (site / plot), with three grouped bars — formulas M1–M3. Plots are ordered by their M1 AGB. Unlike a per-site mean, this shows every plot’s estimate and the real spread within each region.
biomass.variability_desc: Box plot of each site's plot-level AGB for the selected formula. All charts use the same Y-axis scale (and the same size), so variability can be compared directly across formulas.
biomass.comparison_desc: Each chart compares two formulas, one plot per point; the dashed line is the identity (y = x). Points above the line mean the Y-axis formula estimates more biomass than the X-axis one. All three share the same scale.
biomass.comparison_m2m3: **M2 vs M3** — Chave w/o H vs Longo

models.title: Prediction models
models.caption: AGB estimate (Mg/ha) from each plot's LiDAR point cloud.
models.no_data: Train the models (src/train_model.py and src/train_pointnet.py) to see hyperparameters and results.
models.intro: Six models estimate AGB from LiDAR, trained and evaluated the same way — **a single pool of plots, each weight 1, no site distinction, with random k-fold (5 folds)** — for a fair comparison: **GBR** (summarized heights), **ABA** (structural canopy metrics), **Random Forest** (same metrics, bagging), **PointNet** (raw cloud), **2D CNN** (rasters) and **3D CNN** (voxels). All predict the target in log space. The comparison below shows which representation pays off most with this data.
models.compare_caption: RMSE/rRMSE in Mg/ha · global R² (pooled across LOSO folds). Lower RMSE and higher R² is better.
models.compare_highlight: Color: green→red gradient per metric — 🟩 best, 🟥 worst (RMSE and rRMSE: lower is better; R²: higher is better).
models.cv_help_global: Computed over all plots pooled across the 5 k-fold folds — each plot counted once, weight 1.
models.cv_help_r2: R² < 0 means worse than predicting the mean. A high R² does not guarantee generalizing to a new region (nearby plots may land in different folds).
models.results_desc: Random k-fold validation: all plots form a single pool, shuffled into 5 equally-weighted folds, not grouped by site. This is the "predict AGB from the cloud/metrics" scenario. Methodological note: since plots from the same region can fall in both train and test, R² tends to be more optimistic than if each region were held out on its own.
models.evolution_caption: RMSE and R² on the TRAINING set as the final model (all plots) trains — GBR/ABA per boosting iteration, Random Forest as the forest grows, PyTorch models per epoch. This is a training curve, measured on the same plots used to fit: R² climbs toward 1 because the model memorizes the data it saw. It does not replace the cross-validation R² above (on unseen plots) — the gap between the two measures overfitting.
models.diag_caption: From cross-validation (out-of-fold predictions: each plot is predicted while in the test fold). Predicted × Observed shows the 1:1 line; residuals (predicted − observed) reveal systematic bias; the learning curve shows test error as the training set grows (whether more data would help); and the evolution shows the error during the final model's training.
models.importance_caption: How much each metric contributes to the Gradient Boosting (top 15). Only available for interpretable models (ABA).
models.variant_gap: Temporal-gap corrected AGB (DBH/height grown to LiDAR year)
models.variant_gap_noout: Temporal-gap corrected AGB + outliers removed (area > 0.5 ha or compactness < 0.6)
models.variant_dimred: Dimensionality reduction — GBR with K height quantiles (no outliers)
models.noout_pending: Outlier-free models still training — they appear here once their metrics are generated.
